title: Customer Care Compensation Guide: Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate
content:
**Compensation rule.** A Crestline Service Recovery eCertificate, an instrument of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers, compensates one documented service failure on a flown segment of the customer's own ticket. Its value is the scheduled amount for the service failure: inoperative seat, entertainment failure, Wi-Fi failure, cabin cleanliness, crew conduct or catering unavailable.

**Elite increase.** For a customer whose Summit tier is Summit Platinum, Summit Diamond or Summit Chairman, the value is increased by the instrument's elite increase percentage before rounding.

**Annual limit.** A customer receives at most 2 service-recovery certificates, counted over a rolling window of 365 calendar days that ends on, and includes, the date the new certificate would be issued. The count takes the customer's own service-recovery credits with an issue date inside the window, whatever their status, and leaves out voided ones. The system record of the customer's credits is the evidence.

**Flown segment.** A certificate is issued only for a segment the customer actually flew, shown by a coupon-flown entry on the source ticket.

**One failure, one certificate.** One service failure on one segment earns one certificate. Several failures on the same segment earn only the single highest amount.

**Limits of authority.** A value above the support-agent limit of 200 US dollars, or a failure outside the listed reasons, is beyond support-agent authority. It is transferred to a human representative as a request no policy covers.

**Not service recovery.** Irregular-operations delays and cancellations are never service-recovery reasons. They are compensated under the ticket rules of Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

## Rolling window, boundary (hypothetical)

A customer received service-recovery certificates on 1 June 2025 and on 20 January 2026, neither voided.

| Date the new certificate would be issued | Window | Certificates counted | New certificate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 May 2026 | 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026 | 2 | Not issued; the limit of 2 is reached |
| 1 June 2026 | 2 June 2025 to 1 June 2026 | 1 | May be issued |

## Several failures on one segment (hypothetical)

A flown segment had failed Wi-Fi (25 US dollars) and an inoperative seat (75 US dollars). One certificate is issued, at the single highest amount of 75. For a Summit Diamond member, 75 increased by 50 percent before rounding is 112.50.
